{"number":1478,"title":"Re-shelve claudinite-tasks by stage: src/ for the code, queue/ frozen as workflow ABI","body":"`packs/claudinite-tasks/` carries ~24 modules at its root. That is sediment, not design: `git log --follow` on any of them shows one event — `a248483` (#1326) copied the whole flat `engine/scheduler/` directory in with `C100`. The pack root *is* the old flat scheduler dir, and `queue/` is the one sub-system that had already been carved out inside it before the move.

## The stages are already separable

An import graph over the pack (tests excluded) collapses to five stages with **exactly one** backward edge:

| Stage | Cross-stage edges |
|---|---|
| schedule — `scheduler-run`, `readiness`, `schedule-board`, `create-work-item`, `tick`, `drain-dispatch` | ⚠️ one: `queue/scheduler-run.mjs:32` imports `pickOrder` from `queue/executor.mjs` |
| execute-code — `code-work`, `code-work-run`, `prework-run`, `secrets-bag` | none |
| execute-agent — `resolve-dispatch`, `validate-dispatch`, `invoke`, `executor-continuation` | none |
| finalize — `converge-item`, `verify-outcome`, `record-exec`, `land-pr`, `deliver-generated` | none (invoked as CLI from prose, never imported by the executor) |
| recover — `janitor-rules`, `workflow-failure`, `task-janitor` | none |

That edge is placement, not coupling. `queue/executor.mjs` (672 lines) hosts two functions that are not executor mechanics: `pickOrder` (ordering policy over the queue, called by the scheduler run) and `evaluatePrecondition` (the contract's evaluator, published through `shared-code/task-contract.mjs` and re-run by both sides). Extract those two and the DAG is strictly one-directional — at which point the `barriers` pack can enforce it pointed inward, with no bespoke check.

The kernel is small and falls out of fan-in: `queue/work-item.mjs` (14 importers), `merge-policy.mjs` (6), `calendar.mjs` / `task-contract.mjs` / `queue/anchors.mjs` (5 each), `run-record.mjs` (4), `queue/leases.mjs` (3).

## What cannot move

Two of these cannot be repaired by a converge, and they shape the whole layout:

1. **Workflow `run:` targets** — stamped into every member's `.github/workflows/` at adoption, the one directory a converge may never push to. Five frozen paths: `queue/scheduler-run.mjs`, `queue/drain-dispatch.mjs`, `queue/workflow-failure.mjs`, `queue/executor.mjs`, `queue/executor-continuation.mjs`. Moving one costs a human-merged PR per member.
2. **`executor.md` and `queue/instructions.md`** — CCR routine endpoints, a per-repo console setting (`adopt-pack` §4b). Moving one needs every member re-pointed by hand.
3. Engine-mandated names: `pack.mjs`, `worldRules/`, `workRules/`, `tasks/`, `skills/`, `migrations/` and the metadata files.

So `queue/` survives as exactly **five one-line re-export shims plus `instructions.md`**, with a header saying it is workflow ABI and may never hold logic again. Everything else internal goes under `src/`.

## `shared-code/` → `src/contract/`, with shims

The barrier's allow list names `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code` as the one path another pack may import (`.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/declared-checks.json`). The nine modules there are all `export *` — 52 lines total — so they curate nothing today; their whole value is being a stable address. `contract` names that better, and absorbs the existing `task-contract` sense rather than colliding with it: what a task must declare, and what another pack may import.

**It needs shims.** `planPackUpdates` (`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs:76`) marks a pack `blocked` when its `minEngineVersion` exceeds the member's engine — **that pack alone is held back while its siblings land**. So a member can hold a new `claudinite-dashboard` beside a blocked `claudinite-tasks`; if the dashboard imports `src/contract/…` and the mount carries only `shared-code/`, that pack fails to load, the mount fails its self-test, the converge refuses to land at all, and the member cannot receive the version that would fix it. That is the #1004 class exactly. So: move the modules, leave `shared-code/*` re-exporting, retire them on a stamp-confirmable precondition — "no member's `packVersions['claudinite-tasks']` predates the rename" — never a date.

Reference inventory: 15 non-test import sites across 5 consumer packs (dashboard ×5, fleet-sheepdog, basics, growth, lifecycle), 17 in tests, 13 prose/config mentions, the barrier's allow-list string (which must name both paths during the window), and one cross-pack path reference in `claudinite-dashboard/test/pack.test.mjs` reading `claudinite-tasks/stubs/…`.

## Target layout

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/
  pack.mjs  README.md  VERSIONS.md  badge.svg
  executor.md                          ← frozen (console routine)
  worldRules/  workRules/  tasks/  migrations/     ← engine-mandated

  queue/                               ← FROZEN WORKFLOW ABI, nothing else ever
    scheduler-run.mjs  drain-dispatch.mjs  workflow-failure.mjs
    executor.mjs  executor-continuation.mjs        (5 one-line re-exports)
    instructions.md                    ← frozen (console routine)

  src/
    contract/    work-items  anchors  task-contract  merge-policy  signals
                 github  delivery  usage-format  wake          (barrier-allowed)
    model/       work-item  leases  calendar  anchors  task-contract
                 precondition ←extracted  merge-policy  model-map  run-record
                 built-in-tasks  discover  dispatch
    gh/          read  write  tracker  read-items
    signals/     collectors + for-task
    schedule/    run  readiness  schedule-board  create-work-item  tick
                 drain-dispatch  pick-order ←extracted
    execute/     loop  apply-status  heartbeat  suspend
      code/      code-work  run  prework-run  secrets-bag
      agent/     resolve-dispatch  validate-dispatch  invoke  continuation
      built-in/implement-request/   (NOT tasks/ — engine-owned, registered separately)
    finalize/    converge-item  verify-outcome  record-exec  land-pr
                 deliver-generated  narrow-diff  deliver-pr.md
    recover/     janitor-rules  workflow-failure
    adopt/       converge-workflows  hash-minute  stubs/

  shared-code/   ← 9 re-export shims → src/contract/, retired on the stamp
  test/          mirrors src/
```

**The invariant:** `src/model/` and `src/gh/` import nothing from a stage; stages import only downward; no stage imports another stage; `src/contract/` only re-exports.

## Also in scope

- `run.mjs` and `slots.mjs` at the pack root are shims for the retired slot scheduler. Nothing in the tree imports either, and `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` guards `engine/**` paths, not these — confirm against fielded history, then delete rather than relocate.
- `README.md` claims `engine/scheduler/*` still exists as shims. It does not; `engine/` has had no `scheduler` directory since #1326.

{"number":1556,"title":"A member owing a withheld delivery reads as "behind", so a fleet baseline reports it as failed","body":"Follow-up to #1545. That fix stops a pack being stamped while it still owes a withheld workflow file, so the record stays in range and the delivery is re-staged rather than lost. The consequence is a member that has converged correctly but deliberately reports an older pack version for a cycle — and sheepdog has no way to tell that apart from a member that is failing to converge.

## What misreads it

`packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/tasks/fleet-roster/drift-issues.mjs`, `classifyFreshness`, compares each installed pack version against canon and returns `behind` on any gap. A member holding `claudinite-tasks` while canon has moved can never read `FRESH`.

Two things follow:

1. **`fleet-baseline` reports the member as failed.** `follow-to-current.mjs` polls freshness until every dispatched member reaches canon's versions, then reports `did-not-converge` for those that did not. A member that withheld a file will not reach them until the *next* cycle, after the apply stage delivers — so a forced baseline reports it as a failure. That is precisely the lever used to push a withheld delivery out, reporting the target members as broken.

2. **The roster opens a drift issue with misleading remediation.** The `behind` fix text tells the reader the self-refresh is not landing and to check the repo's recent scheduler runs. The self-refresh *is* landing; a delivery is pending on another credential. It self-closes once the stamp catches up, having sent someone to look at the wrong thing.

## Why "behind" is not simply wrong

The member genuinely has not received the version — that is the honest reading, and #1545 exists because the opposite reading (stamped, therefore delivered) is what made a broken fleet look healthy. This is not a request to report such a member as fresh.

What is missing is a **third state**. "Converged, delivery pending" is neither `fresh` nor `behind`, and collapsing it into `behind` loses the distinction that decides whether anyone should act.

## Shape of the fix

Make the hold visible so it can be classified rather than inferred: have the member record that a delivery is owed (and for which pack), and give `classifyFreshness` an `owes-delivery` state with its own remediation text. `follow-to-current` then treats it as a terminal, non-failing outcome — the baseline's job is done once the deterministic half has landed and the apply stage is raised.

Worth deciding at the same time: whether a member that has owed a delivery for several cycles should escalate, since that is a real stall and currently indistinguishable from one healthy pending cycle.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1556","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["bug"],"assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-09-01T10:26:57Z","updated_at":"2026-09-01T10:26:57Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

```
! could not reconcile label "claude-automerge": 404
```

Seen on `main`'s run [32368276774](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32368276774/job/96422660810) and on a branch run of #1089 at the same minute, so it is **not** from that PR — it is standing behavior on every run, and has been long enough that nobody reads the line any more.

`ensureLabels(gh, repo, [...QUEUE_LABELS, ...REQUEST_LABELS])` is the caller; `AUTOMERGE_LABEL` (`claude-automerge`) is in `REQUEST_LABELS`. The reconcile is fail-soft, which is why the run stays green — but the label is the asker's merge authorization (`MERGE_IF_NARROW`), read from a write-gated label at adoption. Worth establishing before deciding the fix:

- whether the label exists on the repo at all, or the 404 is the *update* path failing on a label that does exist,
- whether the same line appears on members (it would be the same code, so probably),
- whether anything has ever successfully read `claude-automerge` off an issue here.

{"number":1555,"title":"The staging sweep deletes on "I didn't write it this pass", which is not the same as "it was delivered"","body":"Follow-up to #1545, which fixed the version-stamp half of that incident. The sweep's own criterion is still wrong, and it can reproduce the same silent loss from a different trigger.

## The criterion

`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs` sweeps the staging directory of anything this run did not stage:

```js
const stagedNow = new Set(withheld.map(stagedAt));
for (const stale of stagedFiles(targetRoot)) {
  if (stagedNow.has(stale)) continue;
  rmSync(join(targetRoot, stale), { force: true });
}
```

Its comment states the premise: *"a file staged by an earlier cycle was either delivered or abandoned, and either way the record that staged it would stage it again."*

That conflates two opposite facts. "This run did not stage it" is true both when the file **was delivered** (good — sweep it) and when the record **stopped matching for some other reason** (bad — this is the only copy of computed content).

## Where it still loses content

`appliesTo` on the vars-bag records tests `text.includes(HOLD) && !text.includes('CLAUDINITE_VARS:')`. It goes false for reasons other than a successful delivery:

- the anchor line drifts — the operator hold is renamed, or the wiring converge regenerates the region
- someone adds a `CLAUDINITE_VARS:` comment, or a partial edit
- the executor is momentarily unreadable or renamed, so `applyRewrites` hits `if (text == null) continue`

In each case the record does not re-stage, the sweep deletes the staged file, and — because nothing was withheld — the pack is stamped, putting the record out of range. That is byte-for-byte the #1545 outcome with a different trigger.

#1545's stamp hold narrows the window but does not make the criterion correct; the protection (`stagedNow`) is conditional on precisely the premise that failed.

## The fix

Delete a staged file only when the destination demonstrably carries its content, rather than when this pass happened not to write it. A file whose destination still lacks it is an outstanding delivery, not a leftover.

This needs care with one existing behaviour: `engine-tests/pack-update.test.mjs`'s *"the retired staging directory is swept, whatever an earlier cycle left in it"* covers a genuine leftover from the retired lane whose destination will never match. That case wants an explicit rule (out of range for the right reason), not the current catch-all.

Also worth scoping: the sweep is unconditional across flows, with nothing limiting it to files the pack flow owns.

## Second, smaller gap

An **engine**-flow record gets no hold at all. `flowOf` returns `{ flow: 'engine' }` with no `pack`, and the guard added in #1545 is `if (owedBy)`. Today the engine flow cannot withhold — `engine-update.mjs` passes `env: {}`, so workflow writes are skipped — while it stamps unconditionally. If the engine flow ever gains the withhold lane, it inherits the original bug.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1555","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["bug"],"assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-09-01T10:26:40Z","updated_at":"2026-09-01T10:26:40Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1382,"title":"Retire the deleted slot scheduler's leftovers — its labels, its session-side resolver, its janitor rules","body":"The slot scheduler is gone: `repo-context.mjs` now rejects `taskScheduler.dispatch: "slots"` outright ("the work-item queue is the only dispatch mechanism; `"slots"` named the slot scheduler, which is deleted"). Its surface did not go with it, and it is still ensured, still read, and still capable of acting on issues.

**The labels** (`dispatch.mjs`'s `SCHEDULER_LABELS`): `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-agent-fleet`, `agent-running`, `needs-human`, `workflow-failure`. The task-janitor ensures all five on every run that finds a leftover `[claudinite-task]` dispatch issue, and *re-applies* a ready label to one it judges un-triggered (`rearmDispatchIssues`) or escalates it to `needs-human` (`staleClaimedDispatchIssues`). `workflow-failure` is the one string that must survive — `queue/workflow-failure.mjs` writes it for real — and it is defined twice, once in each module.

**The session side**: `resolve-dispatch.mjs` (its whole reason for existing is resolving which `ready-for-agent`-labelled dispatch a session was woken for), `validate-dispatch.mjs`, and `executor.md`. The queue never arms a label event — `queue/invoke.mjs` fires a routine with a nonce and the session reads `queue/instructions.md` — so none of that participates in a live hand-off.

**What gates the removal**: whether any member still carries an open `[claudinite-task]` issue. While one exists, deleting the janitor's two rules abandons it, and deleting the labels strips them off it. That is a fleet-wide issue read this repo cannot make, so it belongs to the same cleanup pass as #1119's label sweep; the answer it needs is one line per member.

**Overlaps** #1341 (eliminate the task-janitor: fold its recovery into the scheduler run) — if that lands first, the two dispatch rules are deleted rather than moved, and this issue is only the labels, the resolver and `executor.md`.

{"number":276,"title":"Move chrome-extension-release plumbing out of core `.github/` into the pack (vendored into consumers)","body":"Resolves the **RELEASE** item of #270: the reusable release workflows (`.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml` + `deploy-privacy-page.yml`) and the three composite actions (`read-release-config`, `bump-extension-patch`, `report-failure`) live in Claudinite's core tree but exist solely for the `chrome-extension-release` pack. They must move behind the pack that owns them, leaving Claudinite with no release-specific GitHub Actions.

## Decision (agreed with owner)

- **Hosting model: vendor into each consumer.** GitHub only resolves reusable workflows/composite actions from a repo's own `.github/`, never from a `packs/…` subdir, so "into the pack" means the pack holds the templates and each consumer hosts a *managed* copy in its own `.github/`. Consumers become self-contained; baselining (not the consumer) owns keeping the copies correct. This reverses the original "thin consumer" design — deliberately.
- **Phase-2 deletion: automatic, telemetry-gated.** Once the fleet census confirms every consumer has vendored, the census deletes Claudinite's release plumbing automatically as part of migration retirement — no follow-up PR.
- **Secrets: nothing to migrate.** The four `CHROME_*` secrets already live in each consumer repo (they travel via `secrets: inherit` from the consumer's own workflow); Claudinite holds none.

## Plan

1. **Pack = source of truth.** Move the 4 workflows + 3 composite actions into `packs/chrome-extension-release/` as vendored templates; rewrite cross-repo `uses: missingbulb/Claudinite/.github/…@main` → local `uses: ./.github/…`; rename to avoid the in-repo filename collision (the orchestrator and the create-package reusable are both `chrome-extension-release.yml` today).
2. **Migration is the fix vehicle.** A new baseline migration carries: (a) a **materialize** op — baselining writes the vendored set into each consumer's `.github/` and drops the old thin-stub `@main` refs; (b) a **legacyPresent** probe ("still references `missingbulb/Claudinite/.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*`") for fleet telemetry; (c) a **retire-deletes-from-home** list — Claudinite's own release files. Extend the migration mechanism (today rename-only) with the materialize op, and teach the census to delete the home-repo files on retirement.
3. **Tolerant checks during transition.** The `cer/*` checks accept both the old thin-stub shape and the new vendored shape until the migration retires, so no consumer's check suite goes red mid-flight.
4. **Docs.** Update `RELEASE.md`, `.github/workflows/README.md` (drop the frozen-`@main`-API section), and the pack fingerprint.

## Prerequisite for the automatic cut

The automatic phase-2 deletion needs `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` granted **Contents-write on the home repo** — #239 notes this is not granted yet. Until it is, the census logs "grant FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN Contents write" and Claudinite's copies stay in place (harmless — consumers already run off their vendored copies by then).

Refs #270 (RELEASE item), #239 (token scope).","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/276","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["blocked"],"assignees":[],"comments":6,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-13T14:28:14Z","updated_at":"2026-08-28T01:43:26Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

input.prompt:
You are triaging a batch of GitHub issues in the repo missingbulb/Claudinite, on behalf of the Claudinite "tidy-issues" automated task. This is real production work — actions taken (closing issues, adding labels, posting comments) are live and visible. Follow the procedure below EXACTLY for each issue in your batch. Use ONLY mcp__github__* tools for GitHub access (issue_read, issue_write, search_code, get_file_contents, list_issues, etc.) — do not use gh CLI, do not touch pull requests (no PR reads/writes: this task's scope is issues only).

You may use mcp__github__get_file_contents with ref: "main" to check whether something described in an issue is actually implemented in main's current content — never infer from a linked PR having merged, never from the issue merely "looking done". You may also use Bash/Grep/Read against the local checkout ONLY as a fallback if it happens to already reflect main (check `git rev-parse HEAD` against `git ls-remote origin main` first); prefer the GitHub API for certainty.

The ladder (apply the FIRST that matches, and take exactly one action per issue):
1. Already implemented in main → close it (issue_write, method update, state: closed, state_reason: completed) + post one comment citing where in main it landed (file/line or behavior). Action = "closed".
2. Conflicts with a current guideline (something documented in this repo's packs/ or CLAUDE.md now contradicts what the issue asks) → add label "needs-decision" (create it if missing) + comment naming the conflict. Action = "needs-decision".
3. Blocked by another issue (explicitly, or structurally can't proceed until another open issue resolves) → add label "blocked" + comment "blocked by #N". Action = "blocked".
4. Small and quick to do (a well-scoped, low-risk, single-file-ish change) → add label "quick-win" + comment scoping it in 1-2 sentences. Action = "quick-win".
5. Else → take no action. Action = "left".

Special rule — ticked checkboxes: if EVERY checkbox in the issue body is ticked, that's the author's own claim the work is done. Treat it as a strong reason to run the "implemented in main" check (step 1), never as the answer by itself. If verified true against main → close as in step 1. If NOT verified → post a comment naming specifically what's still missing (do NOT close). Action = "left" for this comment-only sub-case (say in your note that you commented). If the ask has no repo-side artifact (e.g. a console/GitHub setting only a human can flip) — the author's own ticks ARE the closing condition: say so in the comment and close (Action = "closed"). A PARTIALLY ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage as if no boxes existed.

Never re-post a verdict you already posted: before acting, read the issue's comments (issue_read, method get_comments). Find the most recent comment that ends with a line `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->` (or, for an issue triaged before this marker existed, one that clearly reads as this task's own prior verdict). If the action you are about to take is the SAME as that comment's already-announced verdict, do NOT post anything and do NOT change any label — return action = "unchanged", note = "<action> since <its date>". Closing is never a repeat (it changes state), so if a prior verdict said e.g. "quick-win" and you'd now close it, that's a real new action, not unchanged.

End every comment you post with this exact marker, alone on the last line:
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
(substitute the actual action word: closed / needs-decision / blocked / quick-win / left)

Your batch of issues to triage in missingbulb/Claudinite: #1214, #1313, #1322, #1323, #1347, #170, #1341, #1330

For EACH issue, do the full read (get + get_comments + get_labels), decide, act, and record. When done with all issues in your batch, report back a compact list, one line per issue, in EXACTLY this format:
#<n>: action=<closed|needs-decision|blocked|quick-win|left|unchanged> — <one-sentence note, and if you closed/commented/labeled, say what you did>

Do not touch any issue outside your assigned batch. Do not touch any pull request. Do not modify this repo's tracker issues (titled "Claudinite tracker: Tidy Issues" or "Claudinite tracker: Repo Tidy") — that reconciliation is handled separately by the orchestrating session, not by you.

Verified end to end on the canary on 2026-08-14 (evidence on #649): the record's write is withheld to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, rides the PR as a reviewable added file, the update parks at `apply-stage`, and a session moves it into `.github/workflows/` byte-for-byte. So `chrome-release-vendoring` should now be expected to deliver when its consumers converge.

**The vocabulary here is stale.** This issue says "baselining (not the consumer) owns keeping the copies correct" and "baselining materializes it". Baselining was retired in #768 phase 5; the owner is now the pack update flow (`updates/pack-update.mjs`), and the materialize reaches `.github/workflows/` through the withhold lane rather than by direct push — which is precisely why it could not simply be pushed in the first place. Worth rereading step 2 with that substitution before the phase-2 work resumes.

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those
ticks by the issue's own author are the closing condition — say so and close.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left/unchanged).

## Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue
trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again
the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted
— by its marker, or, on an issue triaged before the marker existed, by its wording. If the action
you are about to take is the one that comment already announced, **post nothing and change nothing**
(a label already on the issue included) and return `{ action: 'unchanged', note: '<action> since
<its date>' }`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:

```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```

{"number":1547,"title":"Reconsider the update flow from requirements, not from the existing structure","body":"The update flow needs reconsidering from scratch, in light of:

- #1545 — a withheld workflow file lost silently and permanently when its update PR merged before the apply stage delivered it: the staging / stamp / sweep interplay has silent-loss interleavings.
- The capability split between code-work updates (an Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write `.github/workflows/`) and session updates (credentialed, expensive).
- The update stages running independently (engine, engine-agentic, packs, packs-agentic), each needing different capabilities: coded migrations, agentic fix-code-to-new-standards work.

No existing structure needs preserving; only the requirements do. Freedoms explicitly on the table (owner):

- One update phase, if it can satisfy everything.
- A nightly run guaranteed not to break the build, with the next "apply new guidelines" session fixing tests — acceptable if it buys simplicity.
- Eliminating migrations, or strongly limiting them to `.claudinite-settings.json`.

Approach: one agent derives deployment requirements and limitations (distribution model included, existing mechanisms excluded), a second designs against them from scratch, a third reviews the design against the requirements. Deliverable: requirements + design in `docs/`, superseding `docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md`.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1547","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-09-01T09:24:12Z","updated_at":"2026-09-01T09:24:12Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1050,"title":"Collapse the `needs-human` pair into one label — by 2026-08-26","body":"#1049 landed the triage split **additively**: every park wears `needs-human` *and* one of `task:needs-human-{action,decision,approval,failure}`. Additive was the right shape to land it — no migration, no window where a fielded engine sees an item wearing a label it cannot classify.

It is not the right shape to keep. Two labels for one fact means every writer must remember both, and an item wearing only one is a state nothing defines.

**Do this by 2026-08-26** (one week from the split landing — long enough for the fleet to converge past it, short enough that nothing is written against the pair):

- [ ] Retire `needs-human` as a written label. `task:needs-human-` becomes the state; the four are the vocabulary.
- [ ] Update every reader: `planTick`'s standing-item filter, the janitor's rules (`staleReadyItems` and friends all skip on `needs-human`), the executor's ready filter and claim guard, `dispatch.mjs`'s suppression, the dashboard's `stateOf`/`warningsFor`, `queue-sweep`'s health line.
- [ ] Keep **reading** `needs-human` — open issues parked before the change are stored data, and an item wearing only the bare label must keep reading as a blocking park.
- [ ] Write a migration record that adds the missing sub-label (`failure`, the safe default) to every open item wearing only `needs-human`, so nothing is left in a state the new readers do not recognise.
- [ ] Drop the pair from the prose: `engine/scheduler/executor.md`, `engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md`, `packs/claudinite-growth/scheduled-tasks.md`.

The engine-version bump is the natural carrier for the record. Refs #1049, #1032.

{"number":1545,"title":"A withheld workflow file is lost silently and permanently when its update PR merges before the apply stage delivers it","body":"Five members ended up stamped past a migration record without ever receiving what it delivers, and every signal reported success. The loss is unrecoverable by any later converge.

## What happened

`claudinite-tasks` 60831.6 carries `2026-08-31-executor-vars-bag`, a rewrite putting `CLAUDINITE_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}` into each member's live `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml`. Because a converge's `GITHUB_TOKEN` may not write under `.github/workflows/`, the withhold lane stages it to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` and raises an `apply-stage` terminal; the apply-stage session, holding a credential that may write there, is what moves it into place.

On five members that session parked instead (a separate bug, fixed in `claudinite-lifecycle` 60831.3), leaving the update PR open with the file staged. Those PRs were then merged by hand. That is where this bug starts:

1. The merge lands `.claudinite-settings.json` stamping `claudinite-tasks` 60831.6 — **the stamp advances even though the withheld file was never delivered.**
2. The next converge's staging sweep clears `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, correctly reading the file as a previous cycle's leftover. The staged copy is gone.
3. `migrationApplies` is `want > have` (`engine/checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs:171`). The member is now at or above 60831.6, so the record no longer applies — vendoring stops fetching it and it is removed from the mount.

Net: the live workflow lacks the line, the staged copy is deleted, and the record that would restore it can never reach that member again. Nothing is red anywhere.

## Confirmed state

All five, identically — `CLAUDINITE_VARS` absent from the live executor, `claudinite-tasks` stamped `60831.9`, the record absent from the mount, `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` empty:

- missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary (PR #310, then #311 which shows `removed` for both the staged file and the record)
- missingbulb/hitbut, missingbulb/TLDR, missingbulb/LaughCounter, missingbulb/VascularColoring

The other eight delivered normally and carry the line.

## Why it stayed invisible

- `fleet-baseline` follows members to **canon's stamped versions**, which are current. A forced baseline reported success in 4m35s while all five were missing the delivery.
- The update run itself is green: the deterministic half genuinely did everything asked of it.
- The apply-stage park is the only signal, and merging the PR resolves it — janitor rule G reads the merge and closes the item `task:status:done`, i.e. "nothing is left for anyone to act on", for a delivery that never happened.

## Candidate fixes

Both are worth having; the first is the root cause.

1. **Do not advance the stamp while a withheld file is undelivered.** The stamp is the claim that the member received the version. A run that withheld something has not delivered that version, so it should not stamp it — leaving the record applicable and the next converge able to re-stage.
2. **Do not sweep a staged file that was never delivered.** The sweep's premise is that a staged file is a leftover of a completed cycle. A file whose destination still lacks its content is not a leftover; it is the outstanding delivery.

Either alone would have made this recoverable. Both together also make the failure visible rather than silent.

A test must see the loss happen before the fix: converge with a withheld file, merge without delivering, converge again, and assert the destination still lacks the content while the record has gone out of scope.

## Not in scope here

Re-delivering the line to the five is a separate change — a re-issued record at a new version, whose `appliesTo` already no-ops on the eight that have it.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1545","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["bug"],"assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-09-01T09:09:09Z","updated_at":"2026-09-01T09:09:09Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":1,"references":[{"number":1546,"title":"Never stamp a pack that still owes a withheld workflow file, and re-reach the five members it stranded","state":"OPEN","url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1546","repository":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}]}}

{"number":1538,"title":"The four park kinds conflate two independent questions, and `decision` absorbs the overflow","body":"#1516 fixed two writers that put machine observations into `needs-human-decision`. That was the bug. This is the design question underneath it: the vocabulary made those writers easy to get wrong, and one of them was wrong from the day it was written.

## The four kinds encode two things at once

| kind | what it says the human owes | holds the lane? |
|---|---|---|
| `failure` | read the trace, something broke | **yes** |
| `action` | change something outside the code | no |
| `decision` | choose what happens next | no |
| `approval` | merge or close a PR | no |

Two independent axes are collapsed into one label:

1. **Does this hold the task's lane?** A mechanical property with exactly one correct answer per situation, and real consequences — the generator files no further occurrence while a blocking park stands.
2. **What is a person being asked for?** Routing information for whoever reads the queue.

They are genuinely independent. A dead session both holds the lane *and* asks someone to read a trace. An approval releases the lane and asks for a merge. Nothing about the second axis determines the first, yet one label carries both, so choosing a kind means silently deciding a scheduling question while thinking about a human-facing one.

That is what went wrong in #1515: rules B and D each picked the right *description* — "someone needs to look at this and decide" — and thereby picked the wrong *scheduling behaviour*, releasing a lane that should have held. The description was even defensible in isolation. Only the coupling made it a bug.

## `decision` is the default sink

Its definition is the only one phrased as a residual — "you stopped mid-flight and what happens next is a choice." Every kind's definition names a specific remedy except this one, which names the absence of one. Predictably it collects everything that does not obviously fit, and it is the kind rule E can never clear, so whatever lands there stays. 93 items across the fleet are sitting in it right now.

Note also that `instructions.md` already tells the *agent* that `failure` is the fallback: *"Use this when you are unsure."* Two different defaults for the same taxonomy — `failure` for a session, `decision` in practice for the janitor's own code — is itself evidence the vocabulary is not carrying its meaning.

## Options

**A. Separate the axes.** A park becomes a blocking flag plus a reason. The mechanical question is answered explicitly at each write site instead of as a side effect of naming a remedy. Costs a label-shape migration across every member.

**B. Re-cut the kinds so each names a remedy.** Retire `decision` as a distinct kind; anything currently landing there is either a failure (something broke), an action (something outside the code must change), or an approval (an artifact is waiting). Smallest conceptual change, but leans on the claim that every real park genuinely is one of the other three — which wants testing against the 93 before anyone commits to it.

**C. Keep the four, fix the defaults.** State the lane consequence in each kind's definition, make `failure` the documented fallback everywhere, and add a check that a machine writer never stamps `decision`. Cheapest, and #1516 already does the last part by hand; it leaves the coupling in place.

I have not picked one. **B looks most promising and is the one I would test first**, but the evidence that would settle it is the same investigation now running over the 93 parked items — what each one *actually* was. That should land before this is decided.

## What is already true

- #1516 — rules B and D park `failure`; the janitor writes no `decision` at all.
- `scheduler-run.mjs:385` still writes `decision` and is correct: it fires only for `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'` and genuinely asks a person to choose. Any re-cut has to keep somewhere for that case to live.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1538","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-31T14:16:09Z","updated_at":"2026-08-31T14:16:09Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1328,"title":"claudinite-tasks extraction: delete the legacy shims (gated tail)","body":"PR D of #1317, in #1329. Written and reviewed with the rest of the stack; **merged only at chain link L4**, once L1–L3 have confirmed no member still names an old path.

{"number":1485,"title":"task-declaration-shape passes an unresolvable `automerge` policy, and the task then silently stops being scheduled","body":"`task-declaration-shape` is the blocking world rule that judges a task declaration's shape, and it validates the **value** of every enum field it covers — `frequency` and `agent_model` via `enumField`, `expected_outcome` against `OUTCOMES`. For `automerge` alone it tests only presence:

```js
// packs/claudinite-tasks/worldRules/task-declaration-shape.mjs:66
const hasMayAutomerge = /\bautomerge:\s*/.test(stripComments(text));
```

`hasMayAutomerge` is then used only to pair the field with the ceiling (`pr` without it, `none` with it). Nothing anywhere in the check asks whether the policy *resolves*. A declaration carrying a typo'd rule name, a retired term, or an `under:` scope the member's mount does not yet understand passes the check green.

## The failure that follows is silent, and it is not a parked PR

`discover.mjs` validates for real — `validateTaskDeclaration`, which does call `normalizePolicy` — and drops the task on any problem:

```js
// packs/claudinite-tasks/discover.mjs:67
const problems = validateTaskDeclaration(decl);
if (problems.length) {
  errors.push({ … });
  continue;          // ← the task never reaches `tasks`
}
```

Both consumers render those errors as a bare log line and nothing else — `scheduler-run.mjs:611` and `executor.mjs:630` are each `for (const e of errors) console.log(\`! ${e.what}\`)`. No finding, no work item, no non-zero exit. No world rule reads `discoverTasks()`' errors at all.

So the end state for one bad policy term is: **the task stops running entirely**, with green CI, a green scheduler run, and a single `!` line buried in an Actions log. A task that has quietly left the schedule is indistinguishable from one whose precondition keeps declining.

## Demonstrated

Against `missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite` at `claudinite-tasks` 60830.9, adding one task declaring `automerge: ['under:site/data && typo-not-a-rule-name!!']`:

```
probe task discovered? false
errors: …/task.mjs is not a valid task declaration: "automerge" is not a legal policy:
        "under:site/data && typo-not-a-rule-name!!" is not a policy term …

$ node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
0 blocking, 1 advisory (world scope: all vs origin/main)
```

This was a live near-miss, not a hypothetical. ClaudiniteWebsite#375 landed `automerge: [\`under:${PROMOTED_DIR}\`]` while that member's mount still predated #1474 — `validateTaskDeclaration` returned a problem against the mount as it stood, so the weekly `site-stats` recount would have dropped out of discovery, while `check_the_world.mjs` reported 0 blocking on the branch and in CI. It came right only because the member's mount converged to 60830.9 a few hours later. A member on a slower converge, or a term that never becomes valid, gets no such rescue.

## Two ways to close it, and why I'd pick the second

**Resolve the policy inside `task-declaration-shape`.** Natural, but it fights the check's nature: it is a text scan, deliberately, so it never executes member code. Policies are not reliably literal — canon's own flagship example is now

```js
// packs/product-wiki/tasks/wiki-growth/task.mjs:36
automerge: [`under:${WIKI_ROOT} && doc-changes`],
```

a template literal over a module const, and ClaudiniteWebsite's `site-stats` has the same shape. A static extractor would have to skip exactly the computed cases most likely to drift, so it would pass the very declarations worth catching.

**Surface `discoverTasks()`' errors as findings.** That path already validates with full fidelity — it imports the module, so template literals and consts are resolved — and today its output is thrown away in a log line. One world rule that runs discovery and reports each error turns every class of invalid declaration, `automerge` included, into a blocking finding at author time, and needs no new validation logic. It also closes the same hole for the other fields, since any `validateTaskDeclaration` problem currently disappears the same way.

Worth deciding too whether a scheduler or executor run that dropped a task should exit non-zero, or file a work item, rather than logging past it — a member whose task silently left the schedule has no other signal that anything is wrong.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1485","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"assignees":[],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-30T22:19:19Z","updated_at":"2026-08-31T11:09:54Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

You are triaging a batch of GitHub issues in the repo missingbulb/Claudinite, on behalf of the Claudinite "tidy-issues" automated task. This is real production work — actions taken (closing issues, adding labels, posting comments) are live and visible. Follow the procedure below EXACTLY for each issue in your batch. Use ONLY mcp__github__* tools for GitHub access (issue_read, issue_write, search_code, get_file_contents, list_issues, etc.) — do not use gh CLI, do not touch pull requests (no PR reads/writes: this task's scope is issues only).

You may use mcp__github__get_file_contents with ref: "main" to check whether something described in an issue is actually implemented in main's current content — never infer from a linked PR having merged, never from the issue merely "looking done". You may also use Bash/Grep/Read against the local checkout ONLY as a fallback if it happens to already reflect main (check `git rev-parse HEAD` against `git ls-remote origin main` first); prefer the GitHub API for certainty.

The ladder (apply the FIRST that matches, and take exactly one action per issue):
1. Already implemented in main → close it (issue_write, method update, state: closed, state_reason: completed) + post one comment citing where in main it landed (file/line or behavior). Action = "closed".
2. Conflicts with a current guideline (something documented in this repo's packs/ or CLAUDE.md now contradicts what the issue asks) → add label "needs-decision" (create it if missing) + comment naming the conflict. Action = "needs-decision".
3. Blocked by another issue (explicitly, or structurally can't proceed until another open issue resolves) → add label "blocked" + comment "blocked by #N". Action = "blocked".
4. Small and quick to do (a well-scoped, low-risk, single-file-ish change) → add label "quick-win" + comment scoping it in 1-2 sentences. Action = "quick-win".
5. Else → take no action. Action = "left".

Special rule — ticked checkboxes: if EVERY checkbox in the issue body is ticked, that's the author's own claim the work is done. Treat it as a strong reason to run the "implemented in main" check (step 1), never as the answer by itself. If verified true against main → close as in step 1. If NOT verified → post a comment naming specifically what's still missing (do NOT close). Action = "left" for this comment-only sub-case (say in your note that you commented). If the ask has no repo-side artifact (e.g. a console/GitHub setting only a human can flip) — the author's own ticks ARE the closing condition: say so in the comment and close (Action = "closed"). A PARTIALLY ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage as if no boxes existed.

Never re-post a verdict you already posted: before acting, read the issue's comments (issue_read, method get_comments). Find the most recent comment that ends with a line `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->` (or, for an issue triaged before this marker existed, one that clearly reads as this task's own prior verdict). If the action you are about to take is the SAME as that comment's already-announced verdict, do NOT post anything and do NOT change any label — return action = "unchanged", note = "<action> since <its date>". Closing is never a repeat (it changes state), so if a prior verdict said e.g. "quick-win" and you'd now close it, that's a real new action, not unchanged.

End every comment you post with this exact marker, alone on the last line:
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
(substitute the actual action word: closed / needs-decision / blocked / quick-win / left)

For EACH issue, do the full read (get + get_comments + get_labels), decide, act, and record. When done with all issues in your batch, report back a compact list, one line per issue, in EXACTLY this format:

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and author the canon packs those facets earn. Use from a canon when a project's evidence shows a facet its shelf does not yet home — the curation stages' pack-writing method, and an owner's when asking what a project has taught the shelf.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the tidy-repo pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production long enough to judge — is it working, misused, overused, underused — read from its real production record against expectations written down when the element was designed. Use when designing a larger element (the brief is authored then), when filing a migration plan's chain (the retrospective is its last link), when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/single-issue-triage

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those
ticks by the issue's own author are the closing condition — say so and close.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left/unchanged).

## Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue
trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again
the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted
— by its marker, or, on an issue triaged before the marker existed, by its wording. If the action
you are about to take is the one that comment already announced, **post nothing and change nothing**
(a label already on the issue included) and return `{ action: 'unchanged', note: '<action> since
<its date>' }`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:

```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```

{"number":1264,"title":"Delete the two-name settings-file tolerance once no member carries .claudinite-checks.json","body":"Phase 3 of #1252. The rename landed with every reader in the corpus accepting **both** settings-file names, because a member renames its own file only on the converge that carries `engine/migrations/2026-08-23-settings-file-rename`. This issue is the removal of that tolerance.

## The precondition — a converge-cycle fact, never a date

Do not open this on a calendar. The condition is: **no member still carries `.claudinite-checks.json`**, confirmed by reading the fleet's own artifacts rather than assumed from elapsed time. Retiring a tolerance while a member is still on the old shape does not just leave that member behind — every reader then finds no settings file at all, which reads as "declares no packs, never adopted", silently, with green runs to show for it (the same class as #1106).

The sheepdog roster walk already reads each member's declaration under both names, so the cheapest confirmation is to have it report which name each member answered on.

## What comes out

- `engine/settings-file.mjs`: `LEGACY_SETTINGS_FILE`, and `SETTINGS_FILES` collapses to the one name. Everything downstream that maps over it becomes a single path.
- `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs`: `LEGACY_CONFIG_KEYS` (`claudinite`, `maintenance`) and the two fold-in branches that read them — the legacy `packVersions` map, `claudinite.engineVersion`, and `maintenance.delivery` → `dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview`. A member still declaring either then gets the unknown-setting error, which is correct once none does.
- `engine/installed-versions.mjs`: `LEGACY_STAMP_KEY` and its read path.
- `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs`: `LEGACY_ENDPOINTS_KEY`, and `SCHEDULE_KEYS` drops `endpoints`.
- `engine/scheduler/land-pr.mjs`: `resolveDelivery`, `deliveryFromChecks`, and `deliveryFor`'s `maintenance.delivery` fallback — gated separately on no fielded vendored worker still importing them (walk the trunk's pack history, per the `updates/*` rule).
- `engine/served-by.mjs`: same gate, same walk. Nothing in canon calls it now.
- The both-name reads in `fleet-api.mjs`, `fleet-reads.mjs`, `signals/fleet.mjs`, `packs/claudinite-dashboard/settings-read.mjs`, `seeds-agree.mjs`, `adopt-pack/checks.mjs`, `selftest.mjs`, and the older migration records that read the declaration.
- The `legacy-settings-name` rehearsal fixture, and the assertion in `rehearsal.test.mjs` that requires exactly one fixture to carry the retired name.
- The retired name in the two `except` lists (`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/declared-checks.json`, `packs/product-wiki/declared-checks.json`), the dashboard stub's `paths:`/`hashFiles`, and the `find` in `environment-setup-command.sh`.

The last three are the ones to check by hand rather than by grep: a stub is copied into a member once and never re-copied, and the setup script is pasted into a container by hand, so both outlive a member's converge by an unknown margin. They come out last, or not at all.

{"number":1347,"title":"Merge the dispatch simulator into the scheduler codebase — the sim becomes a test harness","body":"`packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/sim.mjs` (1310 lines) imports **nothing** from the engine: it is a second implementation of the dispatch mechanism beside `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/`. Now that the design is shipped (§17's cadence included), the model no longer runs ahead of the code, so the duplication buys nothing and can drift silently. Fold it: keep the harness, delete the model, and drive the **real** modules from it.

## The drift surface

| sim.mjs | engine |
|---|---|
| `mostRecentAnchor` / `nextAnchor` / `periodMs` / `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES` | `queue/anchors.mjs`, `calendar.mjs` (its own comment says "mirroring") |
| `statusOf` + the legacy-label decode | `queue/work-item.mjs` |
| `writeBoardRow` / `boardRow` | `queue/schedule-board.mjs` |
| `schedulerRun()` — four jobs, both occurrence guards, adoption, reclaim | `planSchedulerRun` + the shell in `queue/scheduler-run.mjs` |
| `pickable()`, `claim()`, `postClaimVerify()` | `pickOrder`, `claimWinner`, `conflictsWithEarlierClaim` |
| `janitor()` | `queue/janitor-rules.mjs` |
| `eligible` / `gatedModel` / `APPROVAL_RE` | `built-in-tasks.mjs`'s `APPROVAL_RE`, `parseRequestFields` |

## Why it is feasible

- Every GitHub call in `queue/` goes through one function — `gh(path, { method, body })` from `signals/gh.mjs` — over 19 distinct paths (issues, labels, comments, permission, Actions variables, workflow dispatch).
- A fake GitHub at exactly that seam already exists in `test/queue/executor-loop.test.mjs` (~45 lines) and already drives the real `runExecutor` end to end.
- `runExecutor` is already fully injectable: `now`, `random`, `heldNow`, `collectSignalsFor`, `runTaskCodeWork`, `invokeAgent`, `log`.
- The pure cores are already exported: `planSchedulerRun`, `pickOrder`, `claimWinner`, `noGoPlan`, `evaluatePrecondition`, the janitor rules.

The enabling gap: `scheduler-run.mjs`'s shell (`main`, exported as `runSchedulerRun`) is argless — it reads `process.cwd()`, `process.env`, `new Date()`, `makeGh()`. Same for the janitor and drain-dispatch shells. They need `runExecutor`'s parameter shape, with `main()` as the argless wrapper.

## What survives — the harness proper

- the virtual clock and ordered event queue (`seq` modelling comment-id order);
- the platform behaviours: the cron grid / `cronHours`, dropped and late fires, stale snapshots for `raceExecutorsAt`, `eventLost`, the absent/corrupt board, `gone`/`unreadable` issues, the collaborator permission table;
- `actionExecutions()`, which gets stronger: the fake counts the engine's real `workflow_dispatch` calls instead of the model's own runs;
- the scenario DSL — 12 methods across 1994 lines of `scenarios.test.mjs`, whose assertions mostly read the issue store the fake GitHub also has, so most scenarios should port largely intact;
- the README's coverage map and "The unsimulated world" table — the second one becomes literally "what the fake `gh` does not do".

## The cost, accepted deliberately

Two independent expressions of the design can disagree, and the disagreement is a signal; afterwards the scenarios are regression tests against captured behaviour, not a cross-check of implementation against spec. That independence is already given up by the standing rule (*"model what the engine's code actually writes, never the rule's stated intent"*), and the design is shipped, so the oracle role has lapsed. Consequence to land in the same change: the sim README's "change the simulator first" becomes "write the engine's pure core first, drive it from the harness".

## Phasing (one PR per slice)

1. Promote the fake GitHub out of `executor-loop.test.mjs` into a shared world (issue store, comment ids, labels, permission API, Actions variables, dispatch capture), plus the clock and event queue. No behaviour change — the existing loop test proves the fake still works.
2. Give the scheduler-run, janitor and drain shells `runExecutor`'s injectable shape; `main()` becomes the argless wrapper.
3. Port scenarios in slices, deleting the matching sim model as each goes green: anchors, then the board, pick/claim, janitor, requests, the executions accounting last.
4. `sim.mjs` ends as world + DSL only; `coverage.test.mjs` and the README tables carry over.

Each slice is red-first by construction: it fails where the engine and the model disagreed, and that failure is the finding.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1347","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-24T19:02:36Z","updated_at":"2026-08-24T19:02:36Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":170,"title":"Revisit: Workflow tool's interactive opt-in blocks unattended routines (waiting on Anthropic)","body":"## The limitation

The multi-agent-orchestration **`Workflow`** tool requires an **interactive human opt-in on every run** ("Allow Claude to run a workflow?"). That prompt only disappears under bypass-permissions / headless modes a scheduler can't be relied on to be in. Because an unattended routine has no human to click **Allow**, any routine that fans out through the Workflow tool stalls on step one.

This also means the tool's nicest ergonomics are off-limits to us for unattended work: committing a Workflow script and having the nightly job just run it by name (`Workflow({name: ...})`) hits the **same** prompt — the gate is on *invoking* a workflow, not on authoring one. And the parallel-agent step can't be pushed into a plain committed script either, since spawning Claude subagents is a harness capability, not something arbitrary code can call.

## Our current workaround

We fan the fleet daily maintenance routine out with **plain subagent dispatch** (the Agent/Task tool) instead, which carries no opt-in gate, and the orchestrator honors the phase barriers itself. See #168 / #169 and `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` + `skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`.

This works and is the right default (no dependency on an out-of-repo permission-mode setting), but it costs us the Workflow tool's built-in phase/barrier machinery and the option to run committed, reviewed orchestration code.

## Why keep this open

This is a limitation of the platform, not our code — we're **waiting on the world to change**. If Anthropic later lets an unattended session pre-authorize the Workflow tool (a settings allowlist entry, an environment/routine permission mode that reliably suppresses just this prompt, or persisted per-workflow consent that survives a fresh cloud clone), we could reconsider using committed Workflow scripts for the fleet routine and get determinism + review back.

**Action:** periodically check with Anthropic / the Claude Code release notes whether the Workflow tool can be pre-authorized for unattended sessions. When it can, revisit the plain-dispatch decision in the routine spec.

We hit the same wall from the other side (Desktop scheduled tasks, 6 machines), and there is one property of the platform that may unblock you without waiting on Anthropic.

Approvals are stored **on the scheduled task**, not on the run and not on the settings file. The app says so in its own `create_scheduled_task` / `update_scheduled_task` tool result:

> Tool approvals granted during a run are stored on the task and auto-applied to future runs.

So for a prompt that a scheduler cannot click, the workaround is to click it **once, by hand, on a task you then never throw away**:

1. create the routine task once and run it manually ("Run now") with a human present — approve the Workflow opt-in there;
2. from then on never create a fresh task for that job. Re-point the same warm task at new work with `update_scheduled_task(taskId=…, prompt=…, description=…, fireAt=…)`. Measured on our side today: the update path raises no dialog at all, and a one-time task fires immediately (the several-minute dispatch delay applies only to recurring ones);
3. if you worry the reused task shows up under a stale name — have the seed prompt call `set_session_title` on its first turn. Verified: the session then appears under its real name (`titleSource: tool`).

The catch worth knowing before you build on it: it is per-task and invisible. A new task is cold and re-asks for everything, and nothing tells you which of your tasks are cold until one stalls. That part is auditable from disk — each task-spawned session records `scheduledTaskId` and `permissionMode` in `local_.json` next to the task store, so a nightly check can name the tasks that will stall before they do: https://gist.github.com/tonydzi/64183d29eeaa37d7b38a3775012a8c1d (stdlib only, read-only, CC0).

Not a fix for the gate itself — the ask in this issue stays valid. But it may move you from "blocked, waiting on upstream" to "runs unattended, with one human click per task, ever."

{"number":1341,"title":"Eliminate the task-janitor: fold its recovery into the scheduler run, its visibility into the dashboard","body":"## The problem

`task-janitor` is the third responsibility of the task machinery (scheduler creates, executor executes, janitor cleans up). Reviewing its four queue rules, none of them earns a daily agentless task of its own: each is either **harmful**, **noise**, or **already someone else's job**.

Owner's verdict, rule by rule:

**A — stale ready** (`ready` for ~2× its period → clear status, park `needs-human:action`)
> So a valid task that just wasn't executed becomes parked?? This seems like it creates more problems than fixes. And the comments are just noise.

The item is *fine*. Nothing is wrong with it except that no executor got to it. Parking it takes a healthy item out of the queue and holds its task's lane, converting a latency symptom into a permanent stop that a human must clear by hand.

**B — dead agent leash** (`agent-running` idle ≥3h → clear status, park `needs-human:decision`)
> The scheduler can identify that and make the status switch.

Structurally identical to the executor-leash reclaim the scheduler run **already** owns as job 3 of `queue/scheduler-run.mjs` — a deterministic, serialized, hourly label rule. There is no judgment in "idle past a clock bound"; it is the same shape, one label name apart, recovering in ~2h instead of ~25h.

**C — stuck dependency** (blocked ≥2 days with blockers open → comment, labels untouched)
> Another noisy comment. The block is there because it's there. No need to make a fuss.

The rule's own comment concedes it: *"Nothing here is stuck mechanically — it will proceed by itself the moment those close."* It changes nothing and posts a comment saying so.

**D — stateless repair** (open item with no state label → park `needs-human:decision`)
> If we can decide on a broken label set — the scheduler can do it by itself and mark `needs-human:failure` and move on.

A torn label swap is a deterministic label condition. `STATUS_NEEDS_HUMAN_FAILURE` already exists in the vocabulary and is the honest classification for it. This also retires the read-then-confirm dance the rule needs today (added for #1104) — a serialized hourly scheduler run does not race the executor the way a daily sweep does.

## Supporting facts

- `packs/claudinite-dashboard/model.mjs` `warningsFor()` **already independently computes all four conditions** as per-item warnings — stale-ready, agent past leash, stuck dependency, `unlabelled`. The broad-scope health review the janitor logs once a day into a run log is a strictly worse version of a surface that is already live and continuous. (Its warning text currently names the janitor; that goes with it.)
- The scheduler run already carries the reclaim machinery (`swapStatus`, the episode-boundary comment guarding against reclaim livelock, F18) that B and D would reuse.

## Proposed end state

1. **Delete** `packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/task-janitor/` and `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/janitor-rules.mjs`, with their tests and catalog/`built-in-tasks` wiring.
2. **B → scheduler run**: extend the existing reclaim job to the agent leash.
3. **D → scheduler run**: a stateless open item gets `needs-human:failure` and nothing else.
4. **A → dropped entirely.** A ready item stays ready; the dashboard already flags it as `serious`.
5. **C → dropped entirely.** The dashboard already carries the warning.
6. **Dashboard**: re-word the warnings that name the janitor to name what actually acts now.
7. **Legacy slot sweep**: `worker.mjs` also sweeps the retired slot mechanism's `[claudinite-task]` dispatch issues still open in members. Decide whether any remain in the fleet; if none, it dies with the task, otherwise it needs a home or a one-shot before deletion.

## Open questions

- Does anything in the fleet still hold open `[claudinite-task]` slot dispatch issues (item 7)?

You are triaging a batch of GitHub issues in the repo missingbulb/Claudinite, on behalf of the Claudinite "tidy-issues" automated task. This is real production work — actions taken (closing issues, adding labels, posting comments) are live and visible. Follow the procedure below EXACTLY for each issue in your batch. Use ONLY mcp__github__* tools for GitHub access (issue_read, issue_write, search_code, get_file_contents, list_issues, etc.) — do not use gh CLI, do not touch pull requests (no PR reads/writes: this task's scope is issues only).

You may use mcp__github__get_file_contents with ref: "main" to check whether something described in an issue is actually implemented in main's current content — never infer from a linked PR having merged, never from the issue merely "looking done". You may also use Bash/Grep/Read against the local checkout ONLY as a fallback if it happens to already reflect main (check `git rev-parse HEAD` against `git ls-remote origin main` first); prefer the GitHub API for certainty.

The ladder (apply the FIRST that matches, and take exactly one action per issue):
1. Already implemented in main → close it (issue_write, method update, state: closed, state_reason: completed) + post one comment citing where in main it landed (file/line or behavior). Action = "closed".
2. Conflicts with a current guideline (something documented in this repo's packs/ or CLAUDE.md now contradicts what the issue asks) → add label "needs-decision" (create it if missing) + comment naming the conflict. Action = "needs-decision".
3. Blocked by another issue (explicitly, or structurally can't proceed until another open issue resolves) → add label "blocked" + comment "blocked by #N". Action = "blocked".
4. Small and quick to do (a well-scoped, low-risk, single-file-ish change) → add label "quick-win" + comment scoping it in 1-2 sentences. Action = "quick-win".
5. Else → take no action. Action = "left".

Special rule — ticked checkboxes: if EVERY checkbox in the issue body is ticked, that's the author's own claim the work is done. Treat it as a strong reason to run the "implemented in main" check (step 1), never as the answer by itself. If verified true against main → close as in step 1. If NOT verified → post a comment naming specifically what's still missing (do NOT close). Action = "left" for this comment-only sub-case (say in your note that you commented). If the ask has no repo-side artifact (e.g. a console/GitHub setting only a human can flip) — the author's own ticks ARE the closing condition: say so in the comment and close (Action = "closed"). A PARTIALLY ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage as if no boxes existed.

Never re-post a verdict you already posted: before acting, read the issue's comments (issue_read, method get_comments). Find the most recent comment that ends with a line `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->` (or, for an issue triaged before this marker existed, one that clearly reads as this task's own prior verdict). If the action you are about to take is the SAME as that comment's already-announced verdict, do NOT post anything and do NOT change any label — return action = "unchanged", note = "<action> since <its date>". Closing is never a repeat (it changes state), so if a prior verdict said e.g. "quick-win" and you'd now close it, that's a real new action, not unchanged.

End every comment you post with this exact marker, alone on the last line:
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
(substitute the actual action word: closed / needs-decision / blocked / quick-win / left)

Your batch of issues to triage in missingbulb/Claudinite: #748, #722, #1072, #1010, #1078, #394, #334, #590

For EACH issue, do the full read (get + get_comments + get_labels), decide, act, and record. When done with all issues in your batch, report back a compact list, one line per issue, in EXACTLY this format:
#<n>: action=<closed|needs-decision|blocked|quick-win|left|unchanged> — <one-sentence note, and if you closed/commented/labeled, say what you did>

Do not touch any issue outside your assigned batch. Do not touch any pull request. Do not modify this repo's tracker issues (titled "Claudinite tracker: Tidy Issues" or "Claudinite tracker: Repo Tidy") — that reconciliation is handled separately by the orchestrating session, not by you.
